title: Feedback That Changes What People Do

narration: Imagine Nina, after Theo's project update.
Great job, she says.
Maybe tighten it up a bit.
on_screen: Great job, maybe tighten it up a bit
beats.visual_intent: A cartoon meeting room as people leave. Nina stops by Theo's seat; her comment appears as a speech bubble between them.

grounding.claim: Nina, Theo and the update are an illustrative scene

narration: Theo smiles.
Next week, the update runs just as long.
Nothing changed.
beats.visual_intent: Same room, a week later. Theo at the screen, slides stacking up; the budget question slide sits last and the wall clock is past the hour.

grounding.claim: Theo repeats the same update the following week

narration: You have probably been Theo.
Kind words, and no idea what to change.
beats.visual_intent: The speech bubble drifts to an everyday desk where a figure seen from behind reads the same kind, empty comment on their screen.

grounding.claim: The viewer has likely received kind but vague feedback

narration: That comment gave a feeling, not a target.
Feedback tends to work
when it names an action to repeat or change.
beats.visual_intent: The vague bubble beside an empty target board with no dart on it: a warm glow on one side, nothing to aim at on the other.

grounding.claim: A comment changes behaviour when the person can tell which action to repeat or change; vague comments tend to leave behaviour where it was
Task-focused feedback tends to be more useful than general praise

beats.misconception: A warm, general comment is enough to change what someone does.

narration: I have said that exact line myself.
Let's rebuild it, one part at a time.
beats.visual_intent: The presenter beside the paused meeting scene, gesturing to Nina's bubble as if inviting the viewer to work on it together.

grounding.claim: The mentor narrator admits to having given vague feedback, as persona framing

narration: The tempting fix is a label.
Theo, you ramble.
But labels tend to make people defensive.
beats.visual_intent: A tag reading You ramble slaps onto Theo's chest. Theo folds his arms and leans back; a thin wall rises between him and Nina.

grounding.claim: A trait label is a conclusion drawn from behaviour, not the behaviour itself
A comment about character tends to prompt defensiveness

beats.misconception: Naming the trait is the clearest, most honest feedback.

narration: Say what you saw instead.
On Tuesday, the budget question came last,
after every other workstream.
on_screen: Tuesday: budget question on the last slide
beats.visual_intent: The label peels off Theo. Nina's bubble rewrites itself into the behaviour line while a small replay of Tuesday's slide stack shows the budget slide arriving last.

grounding.claim: Behaviour is what someone visibly did or said, which another person could have seen or heard
Describing what you observed gives the person something specific to recognise

narration: Now you.
What is that comment still missing?
beats.visual_intent: The behaviour line holds still with two empty dashed slots after it, pulsing gently while the viewer thinks.

grounding.claim: Prompt to predict what the comment still lacks

recall.prompt: Nina's comment now says what Theo did. What does it still not tell him?

narration: What it caused.
We ran out of time,
and the decision slipped a week.
on_screen: Effect: budget decision moved to next week
beats.visual_intent: The first dashed slot fills with the effect line. Beside it a wall calendar flips and the budget decision card slides from this week to next.

grounding.claim: Naming the effect on others or the work shows why it matters; it should be something actually seen

narration: Then one concrete step.
Could you open with the decision you need?
Then agree it together.
beats.visual_intent: The second slot fills with the step. Nina and Theo turn toward each other at the table; Theo nods and adds a note of his own to it.

grounding.claim: Specific goals tend to lead to better performance than vague ones
A next step agreed in a two-way conversation is more likely to be carried out

narration: What he did, what it caused, one step.
Specific, and still kind.
And say it soon, while it's fresh.
beats.visual_intent: The complete comment sits large, its three parts lighting up in three calm colours as each is said; the old vague bubble is a faint ghost behind it.

grounding.claim: The comment names behaviour, effect and one step
Specificity is separate from tone
Feedback is easier to use soon after the moment, while both remember the specifics

narration: Your turn. A report lands Friday night.
A. Be more organised.
B. It came Friday night,
so the team worked the weekend.
Could we try a Thursday draft?
C. Same facts, but be more careful.
beats.visual_intent: A report arriving in an inbox on Friday night, then three answer cards sliding in one at a time as each is read, none marked.

grounding.claim: The late report is an illustrative scenario

options: B: The report came Friday night, so the team worked the weekend. Could we try a Thursday draft?
C: The report came Friday night, so the team worked the weekend. Please be more careful.

narration: It is B.
What happened, what it caused, one step.
beats.visual_intent: Card B lifts forward and gains three ticks in the same three colours as Nina's comment.

grounding.claim: B names observed behaviour, its effect and one concrete step

recall.answer: B names what happened, what it caused, and one step to try, offered as a question to agree.

narration: C sounds complete, but has no real step.
A is only a label.
beats.visual_intent: Card C with two ticks and an empty third slot circled; card A with no ticks at all.

grounding.claim: A vague instruction like be more careful is not a concrete step
A trait label is a conclusion, not a behaviour

beats.misconception: Naming behaviour and effect is enough without a concrete step.

narration: Now yours.
Pick one comment you owe this week,
and rebuild it before you say it.
beats.visual_intent: A sticky note on a monitor with a vague comment; it is crossed out and three empty coloured slots appear beneath it, ready to fill.

grounding.claim: The viewer rebuilds a real comment using behaviour, effect and one step

narration: Back to Theo.
Next update, the decision comes first.
Specific feedback makes change easier,
not certain.
beats.visual_intent: The opening meeting room again: the budget slide now first in Theo's stack, hands raised to decide, the clock well before the hour; Nina's three-colour comment small in the corner.

grounding.claim: Theo's next update changes after the rebuilt comment
Specific, task-focused feedback tends to be more useful, without guaranteeing change
